newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: OCBC not reopening Pacific Bank talks.
newsitem.headline: OCBC not reopening Pacific Bank talks.

text.p: Singapore's OCBC Bank group will not reopen merger talks with Malaysia's Pacific Bank, a senior OCBC official said on Thursday.

"The merger talks with Pacific Bank are definitely off," the official, who asked not to be named, told reporters after the OCBC Bank group announced 1996 net profits rose by 17.2 percent to Singapore $708.9 million.
The two banks called off the talks in January after lengthy negotiations failed to resolve complex issues over legal, accounting and regulatory requirements.
The OCBC official said his bank had not yet decided what to do with its 28 percent stake in Pacific Bank.
"We are waiting for the dust from the merger talks to settle first...before deciding what to do," he said.
He said OCBC was still open to talks with other Malaysian banks, but would continue "full steam ahead" with its fully-owned operations in Malaysia.
The official also said OCBC Bank was not involved in a Bank Negara probe into the dealings of Pacific Bank shares.
Malaysia's central bank is reported to be looking into the usually heavy trading of Pacific Bank shares several days before the announcement last May of a plan to merge the two banks.
